summary: Independent review of branch feat/split-football-data-0.26.0 (6afb0a4) against main (deed324). Packaging-only claim confirmed: the three data files contain the former inline JSON byte for byte, every ?v= equals sha256[:16] of the served file, the branch pages rebuilt with the blocks put back and the 3 read expressions reverted are byte-identical to main, f1/index.html is unchanged, and a side-by-side Google Chrome comparison of main and branch (ko/en x 390/1440) gave identical text for every compared field and pixel-identical screenshots, 0 page errors, no horizontal overflow. All package.json checks that can run here pass; check_release.py passes and fails on each of 13 tamper cases. No blocker found. Should-fix: (1) a failed data file load leaves the page silently broken (no error message); (2) analysis/check.cjs (unversioned, passes on main) and analysis/release-0.25.2/check-core.cjs now crash because they regex the JSON out of index.html; (3) Vercel preview deployment (includeFiles, static data file serving) is unverified. Verdict: merge-ready with follow-ups, provided the Vercel preview check is done before production. DONE means the review was performed, not final approval.

issues.description: If a data file fails to load (404/network), the page breaks silently. Measured by aborting /data/football/data.ko.js in Chrome: 5 page errors ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "data")', 'V is not defined', '$ is not defined', ...), empty upcoming list, empty 'as of' date, no club search box, and no message to the user. Aborting predictions.js: preview and server report still render, the simulation panel is silently missing, 1 page error. On main this failure mode did not exist (data was inline). Low probability (same-origin static file), so a follow-up is acceptable: show an explicit 'data could not be loaded' state.

Checks that regex the JSON out of the current index.html now crash with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading "1")'. Passing on main and failing on branch: analysis/check.cjs (15 checks, unversioned, not a historical release record), analysis/release-0.25.2/check-core.cjs (6 groups, latest analysis core regression), analysis/release-0.25.1/check-core.cjs, analysis/release-0.23.0/check-planner.cjs. None is referenced from package.json, check_release.py, README or VERSIONING, so no official check is broken. The builder's 'only older per-release scripts' wording understates this: analysis/check.cjs is a general engine regression check and should be pointed at server/football-data.cjs (before merge or as the first follow-up). Already failing on main for other reasons (not caused by this change): simulation/pixel-v2 check-integration.cjs and check-roster.cjs, docs/eleven-release-review independent-check.cjs, modeling/prematch-v2-review check.py (missing source file), modeling/odds-0.24.0/check-browser.cjs and analysis/release-0.25.1/check-browser.cjs (timeouts), reports/release-0.25.0/check-browser.cjs (hard-coded Windows playwright path).

Live Vercel behaviour is unverified (no deployment performed). Static review: the function reads only data/football/data.ko.js and predictions.js via server/football-data.cjs (path.resolve(__dirname,'..','data','football')), which matches includeFiles 'data/football/*.js' relative to the project root; .vercelignore does not exclude data/; removing index.html from includeFiles is safe because the API handler 404s every non-API path, so the function never reads index.html. Still required before production per docs/VERSIONING.md: preview deployment check of /, /index.en.html, /f1/index.html, /api/health, /api/report and the 3 data files (status, Content-Type).

Deviation (a), football pages read window.MatchLabData.data.teams in matchlab-shared-search: acceptable with a follow-up. It runs after DOMContentLoaded (readyState check), which fires only after the parser-blocking data script has executed, so it cannot run before the data. check_release.py still proves the football copy equals design/release-0.21.0/search.js after reverting exactly that expression (tamper F fails). Follow-up: when F1 is split, publish one new versioned shared search source that reads window.MatchLabData so all pages carry the same module again.

Deviation (b), '.gitattributes: data/football/*.js text eol=lf': acceptable as is. The ?v= hash and the format check (single trailing LF) depend on raw bytes; tamper H (CRLF ending) makes check_release.py fail, so the rule protects Windows checkouts. git check-attr confirms text/eol=lf on the data files.

check_release.py hashes every tracked file, so committing this report and the review screenshots makes it fail with 'Manifest differs from current release files' until the owner runs 'python3 -I tools/check_release.py --write-manifest'. The reviewer did not modify publication_manifest.json (builder/director-owned).

The local server sends Cache-Control: no-store for the data files (same as the pages). On Vercel, static files get Vercel's default headers (not configured in vercel.json). The SPEC's 'data is not re-downloaded' benefit then relies on revalidation (304). A long immutable Cache-Control for the ?v=-hashed data files could be added later.

Own attack paths (65 GET paths plus HEAD/POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS) against the branch server: only the 3 exact data paths (with any query or fragment) return 200 application/javascript; case variants, trailing slash, '//', .map, %00, ';', %2e/%2f/%5c encodings, double encoding, backslashes and ../ to .env, server/*.cjs, private/ all return 404. '/data/football/./predictions.js' and '/data/football/x/../predictions.js' return 200 because URL parsing normalises them to the allowed file; harmless. HEAD on data files returns 404, same as HEAD on the pages (existing behaviour).
README.md and README.ko.md still say current version 0.25.3 (already stale on main since 0.25.4). VERSION, package.json and the CHANGELOG top entry say 0.26.0.

npm run test:analysis-ui cannot run as-is on this Mac: 'Cannot find module playwright' (not a repo dependency), and the script hard-codes the Windows Edge path. A copy with only the browser path changed to Google Chrome was run in throwaway worktrees with an external Playwright install: PASS 9 groups on both main and branch.

External fonts/logos (cdn.jsdelivr.net, cdn.statmuse.com) were aborted for both versions, so logo/font rendering was not compared. Simulation playback was compared through seeded Math.random and screenshots, not over a full 90-minute playback.
